findings.title: bcrypt.compare competes for libuv's 4 threads
findings.consequence: Hashing runs off the main thread, but on a pool of only 4 threads by default. At work factor 10 each hash takes roughly 65 ms (estimate), so one process handles about 62 hashes per second before requests start queueing for a thread, and file and DNS work waits behind them too.
findings.fix: Raise UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE, run more instances, or rate-limit the endpoint.

At work factor 12 each hash takes roughly 260 ms (estimate), so one process handles about 15 hashes per second before requests start queueing for a thread, and file and DNS work waits behind them too.
findings.fix: Raise UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE, run more instances, or rate-limit the endpoint.

findings.title: idx_users_email duplicates users_email_key on users
findings.consequence: users_email_key already gives the database an index starting with the same columns, so idx_users_email is never needed for reads. Every insert and update still has to maintain both, which costs write time and disk.

findings.title: SELECT follows has no limit
findings.consequence: It returns every row that matches. That is fine while the result is small and slow once it grows (a user with 100,000 followers, an order with thousands of events).
findings.fix: Add a LIMIT (or take/limit in the ORM) and paginate, ideally with a cursor.
